name: Sacred Tooth Relic of the Buddha
what: A canine tooth believed to be the Buddha's, kept in a series of golden caskets. Whoever held it was thought to have the right to rule Sri Lanka.
why: A relic that followed the capital: as Sinhalese kings moved from Anuradhapura to Polonnaruwa, Kotte and Kandy, the tooth moved with them. The Portuguese said they burned it; Kandy says they burned a copy.
now: Sri Dalada Maligawa, the Temple of the Tooth, Kandy. A replica casket is paraded in the Esala Perahera every summer.
dispute: The Portuguese claimed to have destroyed the real tooth in Goa in 1561.

sources.cite: Dathavamsa (The Chronicle of the Tooth), 13th-century Pali text; Culavamsa.
Strong, J. S. (2004). Relics of the Buddha. Princeton University Press.
Wikipedia: Relic of the tooth of the Buddha

stops.note: Tradition says that after the Buddha's cremation at Kushinagar his disciple Khema took a tooth from the pyre. The date of the Buddha's death is itself debated, from about 483 to 400 BCE.
The Dathavamsa says it was kept for centuries in a temple at Dantapura, "tooth city", in Kalinga on India's east coast. Where Dantapura was is uncertain.

In the 4th century, the chronicles say, Princess Hemamala and Prince Danta smuggled the tooth to Sri Lanka hidden in her hair. The king built a temple for it, and the Chinese pilgrim Faxian saw it paraded around 410.
stops.meet: Faxian, the Chinese pilgrim, in about 410

stops.note: After Vijayabahu I drove out the Cholas, the capital moved to Polonnaruwa and the tooth with it, to the Atadage and later the Hatadage, whose ruins still stand.
The tooth passed through several later capitals (Dambadeniya, Yapahuwa, Kurunegala, Gampola) before Kotte, near Colombo, in the 15th century.
Portuguese troops seized a tooth relic at Jaffna in 1560. Whether this was the Kandyan relic, a second tooth, or a copy is the whole dispute.
King Bayinnaung of Burma offered a fortune for it. Archbishop Gaspar de Leão persuaded Viceroy Constantino de Bragança to refuse: the tooth was ground in a mortar, burned and thrown into the river.
Vimaladharmasuriya I brought the tooth to his new hill capital, Kandy, and built a temple for it. The present temple was mostly built by the last kings of Kandy in the 18th century.
stops.meet: a dancer in the Esala Perahera

stops.note: In January 1998 a Tamil Tigers truck bomb badly damaged the temple's front. The relic chamber was unharmed.
